successors.name: Greek Dark Ages
successors.text: the post-palatial Greek world: mainland, Crete and the islands

ledger.x: c. 1750 BCE: the Mycenaean age opens in the Argolid. Infobox 'c. 1750 - c. 1050 BC'; in the Early Mycenaean period (c. 1750-1400 BC) the shaft grave 'became the most common form of elite burial' and gave the period its name. The page gives the type site, not a boundary.

c. 1500 BCE: Mycenaean centres cover the mainland from the Peloponnese to Thessaly. Cliopatria's first shape at its own date; the page names the centres but dates no consolidation ('Mycenaean civilization began around 1750 BC'; 'Palaces proper are datable from c. 1400 BC'; Helladic chronology page: LH IIA 1635-1470…

c. 1450 BCE: a Mycenaean elite takes Knossos and Crete. 'By c. 1450 BC, the palace of Knossos was ruled by a Mycenaean elite'; the page speaks of a 'mainland conquest of Crete c. 1450'; Knossos page: 'After about 1450 BC, Knossos became an important Mycenaean administrative centre.'

c. 1450 BCE: Mycenaeans settle Miletus. Excavations 'indicate the existence of a Mycenaean settlement there already from c. 1450 BC'; presence also reached Iasus and Ephesus. Cliopatria never draws Miletus; its Hittite row covers the Ionian coast from -1300.

c. 1400 BCE: Mycenaean colonists reach Rhodes and the islands. The page: 'Starting in the 15th century BC, the Mycenaeans began to spread their influence throughout the Aegean and Western Anatolia' and 'Mycenaeans also colonized several other Aegean islands, reaching as far as Rhodes'; History of Rhodes page: 'In the…

c. 1315 BCE: Ahhiyawa backs the Arzawa revolt against the Hittites. The page: c. 1315 BC 'an anti-Hittite rebellion headed by Arzawa, a Hittite vassal state, received support from Ahhiyawa'; Hittite records mention Ahhiyawa 'from c. 1400 to c. 1220 BC', first with 'the military activities of an Ahhiyawan warlord…

c. 1240 BCE: Mycenaean settlement reaches the Macedonian coast and the western seaboard. Cliopatria's date for its enlarged shape; the page's sentence is undated (re-read 2026-10-18: 'Mycenaean settlements also appeared in Epirus, Macedonia, on islands in the Aegean Sea', no date). The Troad (contest below) and Lesbos…

c. 1240 BCE: Lesbos passes into Ahhiyawan control. Under Hattusili III (c. 1267-1237 BC) Piyama-Radu, supported by the king of Ahhiyawa, 'later invaded the island of Lesbos, which then passed into Ahhiyawan control'. The page gives no year inside the reign and names no state that held Lesbos before, so the counterpart…

c. 1240 BCE: Ahhiyawan hostility reaches Wilusa. Under Hattusili III (c. 1267-1237 BC) Piyama-Radu's unrest 'may have extended to the region of Wilusa'; the Tawagalawa letter refers to 'an earlier Wilusa episode involving hostility on the part of Ahhiyawa'; the Milawata letter, dated 'around 1240 BC'…

c. 1220 BCE: the last Hittite record of Ahhiyawa in western Anatolia. 'In c. 1220 BC, the king of Ahhiyawa is again reported to have been involved in an anti-Hittite uprising in western Anatolia'; no treaty is recorded, a de facto end. The Tawagalawa letter had implied 'Miletus (Millawanda) was under his control'…

c. 1220 BCE: the Wilusa contest ends with the last Hittite mention of Ahhiyawa; scholars suggest the mythic Trojan War 'could have a historical basis' in this era's turmoil. The Troad stays outside the Mycenaean shapes.

c. 1190 BCE: Mycenae burns a second time and Tiryns becomes the largest centre. Mycenae's second destruction 'in c. 1190 BC or shortly thereafter' ended its status as a major power; Tiryns 'became the largest local center during the post-palatial period'. Earlier: the first wave of destruction c. 1250 BC (Thebes…

c. 1150 BCE: the outer Mycenaean settlements fall away in the post-palatial decades. Cliopatria's date for its shrunken shape; the pages date the palace destructions ('Up to 90% of small sites in the Peloponnese…

c. 1100 BCE: the Mycenaean stronghold at Miletus ends. Miletus page: 'Miletus was a Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor from c. 1450 to 1100 BC' and 'During the collapse of Bronze Age civilization, Miletus was burnt again, presumably by the Sea Peoples' (the burning is undated); Mycenaean Greece page: 'a…

c. 1100 BCE: the Mycenaean world passes into the Greek Dark Ages. The infobox ends the period 'c. 1050 BC' (LH IIIC Late 1100-1070/1040 BC) and the Greek Dark Ages page begins 'c. 1180'; Cliopatria's handover at -1100, the LH IIIC Middle/Late boundary, is kept. wars.name: Late Bronze Age collapse (Aegean destructions)
wars.outcome: Every palace destroyed: Mycenae 1250 (earthquake) and 1190 (fires), Tiryns 1200 (earthquake), Thebes sacked repeatedly between 1300 and 1200, Pylos c.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders: every shape is an archaeological distribution of palatial centres and settlements, and the page says the Linear B texts 'are too fragmentary for the reconstruction of the political landscape'.
